projects.name: LazyEdit

projects.name: Video2Book
projects.summary: A reproducible pipeline that turns rights-cleared video or audio into timestamped transcripts, subtitles, structured notes, PDFs, EPUBs, and multilingual pocket study editions.
projects.reply_context: Use Video2Book when someone needs a reviewable learning package from material they own or may lawfully reuse, not merely a generic video edit. The live Bilingual Lecture Pack is a founding USD 250 service for one rights-cleared English lecture up to 20 minutes, one primary speaker, and either Traditional Chinese or Japanese. It includes reviewed source and translated subtitle files, an editable bilingual source, an A5 study PDF, a 30–45 second captioned preview, a source-rights manifest, and one bounded corrections pass. A complete downloadable project-owned sample is available at https://lazying.art/lecture-pack/#example; it demonstrates the packet structure with a 41.191-second synthetic source, not customer work, independent native review, certified translation, or a full 20-minute delivery. It excludes rights clearance, platform downloads, extra languages, certified translation, dubbing, full-course work, hosting, publishing, and unlimited revisions. Mention the fit check only when the person is choosing a bounded paid workflow; otherwise answer with the public pipeline or sample alone.

projects.name: PaperAgent
projects.summary: A reproducible LaTeX manuscript workflow for clean builds, issue ledgers, baseline-to-revision redlines, figures, tables, references, and submission-template checks.
projects.reply_context: Use PaperAgent for a concrete LaTeX, Overleaf, build, reference, or redline problem. The live Manuscript Build & Redline Sprint is a founding USD 250 service for one LaTeX manuscript up to 7,500 words, one target template, a supplied baseline and revision, three clean builds, an issue ledger, a reproducible redline, and one pass of up to ten consolidated build or formatting corrections. It does not include ghostwriting, new claims, literature review, statistical analysis, peer-review response drafting, submission access, or publication promises. Answer the technical question first and mention the fit check only when the author is genuinely deciding whether to outsource that bounded scope.

projects.name: AutoPublication

projects.name: PocketPolyglot
projects.summary: A Studio, CLI, and reproducible TeX pipeline for multilingual interlinear pocket books, including Wenyan/Classical Chinese with English, modern Japanese, and modern Chinese support.
projects.reply_context: For Classical Chinese, use the user-facing label 文言文 and the maximum-language format: 文言文 main text with English, readable modern Japanese, and modern Chinese. PocketPolyglot is the production pipeline; point readers who want finished public books to the related LinguaLeaf shelf.

projects.name: LinguaLeaf
projects.summary: A public shelf of hundreds of generated multilingual PocketPolyglot editions, including Chinese classics and history in color, black-and-white, and large-font formats.
projects.reply_context: The public shelf includes evidence-backed Chinese-history and Classical Chinese works such as 史記三家注, 漢書, 後漢書, 三國志裴松之注, 資治通鑑, and 春秋左氏傳. Do not claim that every shelf title is graded for beginners; describe them as multilingual reading editions.

projects.name: Leonard Susskind lecture notes
projects.summary: A maintained archive of Theoretical Minimum lecture transcripts, subtitles, notes, TeX, and PDFs.
projects.reply_context: Useful prerequisite guidance: be comfortable with single-variable calculus and introductory Newtonian mechanics; add multivariable/vector calculus and ordinary differential equations as needed, and linear algebra before or during quantum mechanics. The series is strongest as an intuition-building companion, not a replacement for exercises and a full textbook. A common sequence is Classical Mechanics, Quantum Mechanics, Special Relativity, General Relativity, Cosmology, then Statistical Mechanics.

projects.name: LocalLLM
projects.summary: A private local AI studio with Ollama plus a source-revision-pinned, project-local llama.cpp CUDA recipe for direct GGUF and compatible multimodal-projector experiments.
projects.reply_context: The maintained references/llama-cpp.md recipe pins llama.cpp release b10327 at commit 69bf6437914596fbbc4caf09a7ac16f2acdd1a94, verifies the installed server revision, accepts an explicit standalone GGUF and optional LOCALLLM_LLAMA_CPP_MMPROJ, and warns that a projector from another model or revision is not interchangeable. It is a reproducible example, not proof that an arbitrary third-party model/projector pair is safe or compatible.

projects.name: LazyingArt eInk
projects.summary: A multilingual e-paper reading offer connected to free LinguaLeaf books and a free local Kindle sender; the dedicated reader is publicly offered as a USD 128 / CNY 999 pre-order.
projects.reply_context: Lead with the free Kindle sender and free LinguaLeaf shelf when they solve the need. Mention the dedicated LazyingArt eInk reader only when the person is actually evaluating multilingual e-reader hardware. Call it a pre-order, disclose that it is maintained/sold by LazyingArt, and do not invent stock, shipping dates, warranty, battery, display, or fulfillment claims that the public page does not state.

projects.name: WordOrigins

projects.name: L-and-N
projects.summary: A focused English L/N pronunciation coach with Mandarin and Cantonese guidance, minimal-pair practice, and PWA, iOS, Android, and watchOS builds.
projects.reply_context: Use L-and-N only for a concrete L/N sound-confusion or teaching need. Lead with a complete practice method, then mention the free no-signup PWA when it helps the learner act on the advice. The first-party APK and Google internal-test route are test builds, TestFlight build 2 is testing through its public beta link, and neither mobile store listing is publicly available yet. Do not call its score diagnostic, clinical, scientifically validated, or reliably on-device across browsers; recognition depends on the user's platform and browser.

projects.name: LocalKnowledgeTerminal
projects.summary: Private, book-grounded multilingual knowledge cards designed for local hardware.
projects.reply_context: The current public offer is a private-by-design collection-fit service, not a finished RAG application or ready-to-ship device. The free fit check at https://lazying.art/lkt/fit-check/ covers one customer-provided collection, one language goal, intended readers, source rights, privacy needs, sample format, and the customer's existing machine. If the collection is suitable and both sides accept the boundary, the fixed USD 250 founding sprint delivers a written data/privacy/citation map, evaluates an agreed sample capped at 12 source units and 20 test questions, builds up to two cited browser cards when usable, gives a go/no-go recommendation, and includes one factual correction pass. A concrete project-owned example is public at https://lazying.art/lkt/sample-report/; its measured source report remains at https://github.com/lachlanchen/LocalKnowledgeTerminal/blob/main/docs/sample-fit-report.md. It is not a customer result, testimonial, benchmark, sale, or paid-engagement claim. Hardware, shipping, custom OCR, bulk conversion, production deployment, and ongoing support are excluded. Give useful low-resource technical guidance first; mention the sample report or fit check only when the person is genuinely deciding how to handle a bounded private PDF, book, document, or text collection. Never imply that LocalKnowledgeTerminal already provides an off-the-shelf RAG system.
